## Summary

Depends on the published [`@example-owner/deployment` 0.1.0](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@example-owner/deployment) (from [example-owner/ark#118](https://github.com/example-owner/ark/pull/118), released by ark's release workflow with npm provenance), locked in `pnpm-lock.yaml` with the registry's integrity. Nothing of the package is vendored here.

kiro-remote moves from deploying by hand to deploying from `main` through the ark member **deployment**, as longplay's platform does:

- **`KiroRemotePipelineStack`** (`packages/pipeline`), in its own CDK app so the service's deploy never touches it: CodeConnections, CodePipeline V2 with SUPERSEDED, one CodeBuild action (ARM, Docker for the bridge image), the retained ledger table, its own notification topic and a build-failed alarm. The build's role (the runner) assumes a deploy role, a read-only smoke role and one role per deployment task, each trusted by the runner alone.
- **`deploy.toml`**: every name the run uses, the preflight (deploy.sh's guards) and the settings schema from `deploy.env.example`, with the settings whose absence would delete something REQUIRED. `config.test.ts` holds it to `scripts/deploy.sh`'s keys, context names, defaults and required settings.
- **The smoke checks** (`packages/pipeline/src/smoke/checks.ts`), from `docs/deploy.md` and the README, run as a role that cannot read session data. `checks.test.ts` fails when a check makes a call the role is not granted.
- **`tasks/`**, empty, with the protocol in `tasks/README.md`.
- **The policy simulation** (`packages/pipeline/scripts/simulate-pipeline-policy.ts`), with a refusal beside every grant.
- **Provenance:** every function gets `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` (`vcs.ref.head.revision`, `vcs.repository.url.full`, `deployment.environment.name`, `service.version`) from the pipeline's context, and the api, bridge and github loggers put them on every log line.
- **`scripts/deploy.sh` is unchanged** and stays the break-glass path. `AGENTS.md` takes longplay's deployment rules, adapted: agents never deploy; checks and tasks instead of runbooks; `needs-person` for what only a person can do. `docs/pipeline.md` is the runbook.
- **A decision log** (`adr init --skill`), with three proposed decisions: `2n47hfqw` (the pipeline), `bwram7sv` (the smoke role), `x7s3v8da` (provenance). None is accepted here.

## Evidence

All against the published `@example-owner/deployment` 0.1.0 from npm, after deleting every `node_modules` and running `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (passes), on Node 26.13.0 and pnpm 12.18.0. kiro-remote has no CI, so these local runs are the evidence. Each result is the same as the earlier run against a packed tarball of the ark branch; the policy simulation's output is identical line for line.

- **`pnpm check`** (lint, type-check, tests; the settings parity test is `packages/pipeline/src/config.test.ts`, 6 passed): core 182, pipeline 36, auth 124, github 154, api 109 (15 skipped, the emulator tests), mcp 77, bridge 131, e2e 63, cdk 85: all passed. `adr verify`: no findings.
- **The service synth** (`cdk synth KiroRemoteDnsStack KiroRemoteStack` in `packages/cdk`, with deploy.toml's `-c` settings and the provenance context): passes cdk-nag, and all 8 of the service's functions carry `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=vcs.ref.head.revision=9bb4f62…,vcs.repository.url.full=https://github.com/example-owner/kiro-remote,deployment.environment.name=production,service.version=9bb4f62…` (the CDK trigger provider, not the service's, does not). Without the context, none does (`packages/cdk/src/provenance.test.ts`).

- **The pipeline stack's role tests** (`pipeline-stack.test.ts`, 11): V2, SUPERSEDED, a clone of the repository, one CodeBuild action; the ledger retained, deletion-protected, with point-in-time recovery; no `Fn::ImportValue`; the freeze check before anything is installed, then `pnpm check`, then `deploy run`; each work role trusted by the runner only; the runner never deletes the flag or a ledger item; the smoke role has no action that reads data.

## Decisions

- **A decision log for kiro-remote,** started with the published adr 0.7.0 (`adr init --skill`: the log, its template and the skill; not `--setup`, which would also add MCP config, harness hooks and a `prepare` script). biome now skips `docs/adr` and `.claude/skills`: its Markdown formatter rewrote the adr template's front matter and would rewrite decision bodies adr freezes.
- **`GITHUB_APP_SECRET_ARN` is REQUIRED in the pipeline only.** `deploy.sh` treats it as optional, but GitHub wake is deployed (its webhook, queues and functions are in the stack), a deploy without the setting removes them, and the pipeline deploys with no one reading a diff. The test checks that every setting deploy.sh requires is REQUIRED here, not the reverse.
- **No rollback triggers yet:** `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` in eu-north-1 finds no alarm of kiro-remote, and a missing alarm would fail the deploy ([rollback triggers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-rollback-triggers.html)). The deploy role gets no CloudWatch permission until there are; a test says so.
- **The pipeline owns its notification topic** (`kiro-remote-deployment`), because the service has none; `--alarm-email` subscribes an address at the bootstrap.
- **The CDK output directory is `cdk.out`,** as deploy.sh's: the first synth into `cdk.out.deploy` copied itself into the bridge image's build context until the path was too long, because `BRIDGE_IMAGE_EXCLUDES` excludes `**/cdk.out` only.
- **Blank means off cannot be said in SSM** (it holds no empty value), so the pipeline uses the defaults for `CUSTOM_DOMAIN_NAME` and `DNS_ZONE_NAME`. Both are on in the deployed stack.
- **0.1.0 is excluded from pnpm's minimum release age** (`minimumReleaseAgeExclude` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, beside `@biomejs/*`): it was less than a day old when it was locked. The entry names that one version and can go once it is a day old.
- **Provenance reaches the logs through Powertools' `persistentKeys`,** since Powertools reads no `OTEL_*` variable; `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` is what an OpenTelemetry SDK reads if one is added. The value changes per commit, so every function's configuration is updated on every pipeline deploy.
- **The smoke checks use the public API over HTTP without a token** for what configuration cannot show (the OpenAPI contract, the OAuth metadata, a 401 without a token), and no AWS read of a table, object, log, user or secret value.
- **Versions:** `@example-owner/deployment` 0.1.0 (it brings Zod 4.6.7 and the AWS SDK 3.1173.0); for the pipeline app aws-cdk-lib 2.278.0, constructs 10.8.1 and the CDK CLI 2.1149.0, the latest on 2026-11-21. The service stays on its locked aws-cdk-lib 2.275.0 and CLI 2.1148.0, because bumping them changes what deploys and belongs in its own change (2.1148 has both rollback-trigger flags). vitest ^5.1.0 (resolved 5.1.0; latest 5.1.1) and biome ^2.6.6 as before.
- **A root `pnpm check` script** (lint, build, test), which the build runs before it deploys, like longplay's.

## After deploy (`needs-person`)

1. **Store the settings in SSM** from your `deploy.env`: `./scripts/pipeline.sh settings`. It refuses without `KIRO_CLI_VERSION`, `KIRO_API_KEY_SECRET_ARN`, `HOSTED_ZONE_ID` or `GITHUB_APP_SECRET_ARN`.
2. **The GitHub token** for the deployment records: a fine-grained token for `example-owner/kiro-remote` only, **Deployments: Read and write**, stored as `aws secretsmanager create-secret --region eu-north-1 --name kiro-remote/deployment/github-token --secret-string '<token>'`. Without it the pipeline deploys and records no GitHub deployment.
3. **The CodeConnections handshake:** `aws codeconnections create-connection --region eu-north-1 --provider-type GitHub --connection-name kiro-remote-github`, then Developer Tools → Settings → Connections → `kiro-remote-github` → Update pending connection → the AWS Connector for GitHub app for `example-owner/kiro-remote` only. It must read **Available**.
4. **Check the roles** (read-only): `./scripts/pipeline.sh simulate` → `OK: 91 policy decisions and 20 trust decisions match`.
5. **Bootstrap the pipeline stack:** `./scripts/pipeline.sh bootstrap --connection-arn <arn> --alarm-email <you>`, confirm the topic's subscription mail, then `./scripts/pipeline.sh simulate --deployed`.
6. **Watch the first run** (merging this starts it; otherwise Release change on `kiro-remote-deploy`), in `/aws/codebuild/kiro-remote-deploy-run`: the freeze check, `mise install`, `pnpm check`, the settings and preflight, the synth, `rollback triggers ...: none`, the deploy (every function's configuration changes once), the smoke checks all PASS, now provenance too, `no deployment task was pending`, `DONE`. The repository's Deployments page shows `production` active at the commit.
7. **The drill:** merge a commit that adds `add("stack", "a drill: this check fails on purpose", "FAIL", "remove me");` to the first check in `packages/pipeline/src/smoke/checks.ts`. Watch the run deploy it, fail the smoke stage, set the freeze flag, deploy the last good commit again (`rolled back: the last good commit <sha> is deployed again`), mail the topic and end `rolled-back`; GitHub shows the drill's deployment as failure and the previous one still active; `./scripts/pipeline.sh status` says `PIPELINE FROZEN`. Merge the revert: its run stops at the flag. **Unfreeze:** `./scripts/pipeline.sh unfreeze`, then Release change: the revert deploys and passes.

## Next

Out of scope here: moving longplay onto the package; the read-only MCP server; the npm dist-tag target; draft's deployment kind; the release member. For kiro-remote: CloudWatch alarms on the service (the dead-letter queues, function errors), so the deploy gets rollback triggers; the first deployment task, with its role; cdk-nag on the pipeline app; bumping the service's aws-cdk-lib and CDK CLI.
